facts.fact: OpenRouter charges a 5.5% fee, with a $0.80 minimum, when a user purchases credits.
facts.quote: OpenRouter charges a 5.5% ($0.80 minimum) fee when you purchase credits.

facts.fact: OpenRouter charges a 5% fee on crypto payments.
facts.quote: Crypto payments are charged a fee of 5%.

facts.fact: Under the pay-as-you-go plan, BYOK usage up to $25,000 per month has no BYOK fee.
facts.quote: Pay-as-you-go includes $25,000 per month with no BYOK fee, while Enterprise allowances are custom.

facts.fact: For BYOK usage above the plan's free allowance, OpenRouter charges a fee of 5% of what the same model and provider would normally cost on OpenRouter.
facts.quote: Usage above the allowance has a fee of 5% of what the same model and provider would normally cost on OpenRouter.

facts.fact: Enterprise BYOK allowances are set custom rather than at a fixed amount.
facts.quote: Pay-as-you-go includes $25,000 per month with no BYOK fee, while Enterprise allowances are custom.

facts.fact: OpenRouter states that there is no markup on inference pricing, which passes through the underlying providers' prices.
facts.quote: there is no markup on inference pricing

facts.fact: Each model and provider on OpenRouter has its own price per million tokens.
facts.quote: Each model and provider has a different price per million tokens.

facts.fact: The ':free' model variant is a free version of the model that has its own rate limits.
facts.quote: A free version of the model with its own rate limits.
